title: Why Does Lake Natron Turn Animals Into STATUES? 🦩
description:
This lake turns animals into statues. Not stone, though. Lake Natron in northern Tanzania is so full of natron (soda: washing soda and baking soda) that its water is like hot washing soda: up to pH 10.5, nearly as strong as ammonia, and up to 60 °C. It can burn your skin. Anything that dies in it gets dried out and coated in a white crust, so the bodies stay perfectly preserved: basically mummies (photographer Nick Brandt found birds and bats like that on its shore and posed them on branches). Ancient Egyptians made their mummies with the very same salt: natron. And yet flamingos LOVE it: up to three in four of the world's lesser flamingos hatch here, because the burning water keeps predators away from their nests. Would you touch it? Yes or no?
